Reco Raises $55 Million for Agentic Security
The company will use the funds to expand its sales, partnerships, channels, and customer support teams.

By
Ionut Arghire
|
 + Flipboard + Reddit + Whatsapp + Whatsapp + Email
Cybersecurity funding
Agentic cybersecurity firm Reco today announced raising $55 million in a strategic funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $140 million.
The investment round was led by AT&T Ventures, with additional support from new investors Forestay and Quadrille Capital.
Founded in 2020, New York-based Reco provides organizations with an overview of the agents that are active in their environments and the risks they pose.
The company shows security teams which identities the AI agents use, their permissions, what data and which systems they reach, and the workflows they can initiate.
Using the Reco Graph, it maps the relationships between agents and accounts, API connections, sessions, MCP tools, workflows, and employee applications to identify unnecessary exposure, revoke excessive permissions and outdated access, disable risky integrations, and enforce policies.
Reco’s solution integrates with multiple AI providers and enterprise applications, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft’s Copilot, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Workday.

The company plans to use the fresh investment to hire new talent across its sales, partnerships, channels, and customer support teams.
“As both an investor and customer, AT&T recognizes the growing importance of helping organizations understand and manage how AI agents interact with business applications and data,” said AT&T Ventures head Vikram Taneja.
“Reco’s approach to visibility and governance aligns with the needs we are seeing across enterprises as agent adoption continues to evolve,” Taneja added.

RECO launches continuing education course on professional liability insurance
New course arrives roughly a year after RECO's professional indemnity program paid out consumer deposit and commission protection claims tied to the iPro matter
RECO launches continuing education course on professional liability insurance
INSURANCE NEWS 
By   Josh Recamara
Jul 16, 2026
Share
The Real Estate Council of Ontario (RECO) has launched a new elective continuing education course to help Ontario real estate professionals better understand the Professional Liability Insurance Program, their obligations, and the role the program plays in consumer protection.
Through consultation with the sector, RECO identified insurance as an area where registrants would benefit from additional targeted education. The course provides an overview of the three types of coverage under the program, Errors and Omissions, Commission Protection and Consumer Deposit, and covers registrants' insurance obligations under the Trust in Real Estate Services Act, 2002 (TRESA), including scenarios that demonstrate how the program applies in practice.
By law, every registered real estate professional in Ontario must carry professional liability insurance. The requirement is intended as a consumer protection measure, ensuring financial safeguards are in place when a consumer experiences a loss resulting from a registrant's error, negligence, or other covered circumstances. The program also provides coverage to registrants for certain insured losses and claims.
Ontario's program remains distinct within Canada's real estate insurance landscape
RECO's model is unique among Canadian real estate regulators. British Columbia mandates its own equivalent through the Real Estate Errors and Omissions Insurance Corporation (REEOIC), a special-act corporation that provides E&O coverage to roughly 30,000 licensees in that province, but Ontario remains the only province offering commission protection insurance and social engineering fraud coverage alongside its E&O and consumer deposit coverage.
The annual insurance fee for Ontario registrants has held at $500 per registrant since 2022, a cost RECO describes as competitively priced relative to other provinces despite the program's broader scope.
Course follows a period of real-world strain on the program
The launch comes roughly a year after RECO's Professional Liability Insurance Program was tested by the collapse of iPro Realty, in which co-founders were alleged to have diverted trust account funds meant to hold client deposits and agent commissions. RECO froze iPro's trust accounts, allowed in-progress transactions to close, and by December 2025 confirmed no consumer deposit had gone uncompensated, with roughly $5 million in consumer deposit claims paid out by that point. In January 2026, RECO approved 100% payouts of all eligible commission protection claims for affected agents, drawing on the program's insurance stability fund to cover the shortfall.
In response to the iPro matter, RECO has also introduced a mandatory annual financial filing requirement for all Ontario brokerages, effective October 1, 2026, requiring brokerages to report on trust assets, liabilities, and unclaimed trust monies, with further monthly trust reconciliation reporting planned for 2027. Against that backdrop, the new insurance education course adds a registrant-facing layer to that broader effort, and it is in this same spirit of strengthening the system from the ground up that RECO is also revisiting how continuing education itself is delivered.
Modernizing continuing education
Beyond its immediate focus on insurance, the launch represents an early milestone in RECO's broader education modernization effort. As continuing education continues to evolve, RECO is exploring opportunities to strengthen learning outcomes, and the course includes a mandatory assessment that learners must successfully complete to earn credit, a new feature intended to generate insights that will help inform RECO's wider work on modernizing regulatory education.
Executive comment
Jean Lépine, RECO's Administrator and Acting CEO, said professional liability insurance is much more than a registration requirement. "It plays an important role in maintaining trust and confidence in Ontario's real estate services sector," he said. "This course provides practical education that helps registrants better understand their responsibilities, how the program works, and the important role it plays in consumer protection."
RECO is a not-for-profit corporation established in 1997 to regulate real estate agents and brokerages to protect consumers in Ontario's real estate services sector, and administers TRESA.
For an industry still working through the fallout of the iPro matter, the new course signals that RECO sees registrant understanding of the insurance program, not just brokerage-level financial oversight, as part of rebuilding confidence in how Ontario protects real estate consumers.

Company appoints COO and new executive team, opens Texas office, expands into UKI, and earns top national reseller rankings. Recognized with three Global InfoSec Awards.
NEW YORK, June 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Reco, the only AI security platform purpose-built to discover, govern, and secure every AI agent, identity, and SaaS connection across the enterprise, today announced a series of strategic executive appointments, geographic expansion in Texas and the United Kingdom and Ireland, and channel milestones that reflect a market reaching an inflection point. Fortune 500 enterprises are deploying AI agents at scale. The governance infrastructure to manage them is no longer optional. Organizations need continuous visibility across their apps, the AI running inside them, and the agents extending beyond them. More than 100 enterprises are already building that with Reco.
The company has named Zoe Hillenmeyer as Chief Operating Officer. Hillenmeyer joins from Protect AI, where she led commercial and marketing functions across AI security, and brings senior experience from AWS, IBM, and Peak AI. At Reco, she will oversee go-to-market execution, operational scale, and cross-functional alignment as the company expands its enterprise footprint. She joins at a moment when AI agent security is shifting from early adopter priority to mainstream enterprise requirement.
Reco has appointed Kristen Twining as Senior Vice President of Americas Sales and Business Development. Twining joins from FireMon, where as Senior Vice President of Sales Americas she drove and closed enterprise cybersecurity deals across the $1B to $3B segment. At Reco, she will own the full Americas sales motion with responsibility for pipeline growth, enterprise close, and expanding the company's mid-market presence.
Additional executive appointments include Dana Harduf as Chief Human Resources Officer, Sandy Mathews as Vice President of Product Marketing, and Merav Keren Kindler as Vice President of Marketing.
Reco is opening a physical office in Texas, where the company has operated with dedicated team members and enterprise customers. Texas is home to one of the highest concentrations of Fortune 500 headquarters in the United States, with particular depth in financial services, energy, and healthcare, sectors where AI agent adoption and the identity risk it introduces are advancing rapidly.
The company has also placed a team on the ground in the United Kingdom and Ireland. EU AI Act enforcement timelines are creating board-level urgency for AI agent governance, and European enterprise demand has grown steadily alongside U.S. pipeline. Oliver Sears has joined Reco as the company's UKI Sales Director to own enterprise go-to-market across the region.
Reco has reached top national reseller rankings with a key channel partner in the United States. This partner has built a managed security practice around the Reco platform, using it to deliver AI agent governance and identity security services to enterprise clients. The model demonstrates how channel partners can build differentiated service offerings on top of Reco's infrastructure. In addition, enterprise wins are driving inclusion in Q1 reviews and QBRs, and the indirect pipeline is growing in parallel with the direct sales build-out.
The company also received three Global InfoSec Awards in 2026 for Market Innovator SaaS/Cloud Security, Market Leader AI Security Solution, and Pioneering GenAI Cybersecurity, reflecting independent recognition of Reco's technical depth and traction across the enterprise security market.
"What surprised me most was how painless it was — and that's thanks to Reco. We were projecting many hours, lots of responsibilities, more work for our team. And to have a solution that was able to come in and give us, almost instantly, within days, the true understanding of our footprint and our environment was very surprising in a positive way."
— Aaron Ansari, CISO, Exela Pharma Sciences, a fast-growing US-based life sciences company
"I joined Reco because the company is solving the right problem at exactly the right moment. Agent governance is where identity security and AI risk converge, and most enterprises do not yet have the infrastructure to manage it. Every organization I have talked to is at a different stage: some are governing a handful of agents, some have hundreds operating across their environment without full visibility. My focus at Reco is building the go-to-market infrastructure to meet them where they are and scale with them as this category matures."
— Zoe Hillenmeyer, COO, Reco
"AI agent security is no longer a planning-cycle conversation for Fortune 100 security teams. It is an active deployment challenge. We built Reco to be the platform security leaders reach for when they need to know what every agent in their environment can access, what it is doing, and whether it is operating within policy. The executive hires, the geographic expansion, and the channel build are strategically intentional. We are positioning Reco to lead this category as it becomes standard enterprise security infrastructure. We are building the channel and technology partner ecosystem to get there at scale."
— Ofer Klein, CEO, Reco
About Reco
Reco delivers continuous posture across the full stack: your apps, the AI running inside them, and the agents extending beyond them. The only AI security platform purpose-built to discover, govern, and secure every AI agent, identity, and SaaS connection within the enterprise.
Security leaders at Fortune 500 companies choose Reco to bring order to AI agent proliferation and the chain reactions that follow. Backed by a Knowledge Graph that maps identities, permissions, connectivity, and activity in real time, Reco delivers 1,000+ detection controls, deploys in 48 hours, and integrates with leading SIEM, SOAR, runtime, and endpoint solutions. 235+ apps supported, with new integrations built in three to five days. Learn more at www.reco.ai.

Reco Raises $55 Million to Help Companies Secure AI Agents
Tuesday, 29 September 2026, 16:03
At one Fortune 100 customer, Reco says it uncovered 21,000 previously unknown agents, while a separate discovery exposed a surprising route to company data.
As AI agents spread rapidly, the need is growing for tools that help monitor their activity. Startups in this space offer to detect agents, restrict their access to data and software, review the tools available to them, and track system activity in real time.
As reported by TechCrunch
Reco has expanded its focus: the company, which previously concentrated on securing cloud applications and AI platforms, now also tracks agents’ connections to apps, users, accounts, and permissions. Co-founder and CEO Ofer Klein explained that customers are deploying agents faster than they can keep track of them.
According to Reco, the company detected 21,000 previously unknown agents at one Fortune 100 customer. At another large financial institution, it found an agent created by a former employee. The agent had access to Salesforce and could send data to a domain unknown to the company.
Data from other players in the market also point to the scale of the problem. HiddenLayer has more than 50 customers using agents in production environments, while Cymphony found about 85,000 files accessible to AI tools at a publicly traded U.S. company.
Reco raises $55 million
Reco raised $55 million in a financing round that extended its $30 million Series B, announced in February. Investors include customer AT&T, through its venture arm, as well as Forestay and Quadrille Capital. The startup has raised $140 million in total.
Klein said Reco’s valuation more than doubled after the previous round was announced. He did not disclose the company’s exact valuation.
Reco has more than 100 customers, with financial services companies accounting for about 40% of its business, and generates tens of millions of dollars in annual recurring revenue. The company plans to triple that figure. Its platform supports more than 280 applications, and the new funding will go toward hiring, sales, partnerships, and customer support.
Reco’s round comes amid growth in the AI agent security market: companies are increasingly adopting these systems, while startups compete to help businesses detect agents and control their access and actions.

Reco Joins Invitation-Only Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program to Accelerate Enterprise Agent Security
Recolabs Inc.
3 min read
 MSFT
Recolabs Inc.
Recolabs Inc.
Partnership will help more Microsoft customers discover, govern and reduce the risk of AI agents embedded across enterprise applications and workflows
ALTAMONTE SPRINGS, Fla., Oct. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Reco, the leader in Agent Security, today announced it has been accepted into the invitation-only Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program, which helps enterprise-ready startups reach customers through Microsoft's enterprise channels. Reco's participation builds on its existing support and integration with Microsoft enterprise technologies and will help bring Agent Security to more organizations.
MSFT Pegasus Logo
Reco Joins Invitation-Only Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program to Accelerate Enterprise Agent Security
AI agents are becoming part of the Microsoft applications, cloud services and workflows employees already use. As those agents inherit user access and move data or initiate actions across connected systems, security teams need to see the full chain of identity, permissions and activity behind them. Reco gives Microsoft customers that context, helping them discover unmanaged agents, identify risky access paths and remove unnecessary permissions before they expose data or disrupt business operations.
"AI agents in Microsoft environments can inherit access across the identities, applications and workflows companies use every day," said Ofer Klein, founder and CEO of Reco. "Effective agent security connects each agent to its owner, permissions, connected applications and activity so security teams can reduce risk without interrupting legitimate work. Pegasus gives Reco a stronger path to bring that protection to more Microsoft customers and support it at production scale."
Built on the Reco Graph, the Reco Platform unifies agent security, posture management and threat detection. Reco Factory can add support for third-party agents and applications in hours, while Reco Library supplies a constantly growing catalog of more than 280 pre-built integrations. The platform includes more than 1,000 detection controls and has identified more than 1 million agents.
"We're excited to welcome Reco to the Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program. Reco Expands Leadership Team and Global Operations as Enterprise AI Governance Demand Grows
June 8, 2026

As enterprises deploy growing numbers of AI agents across business applications, security teams are facing a new challenge: maintaining visibility, governance and control over systems that increasingly operate autonomously. Reco is positioning itself to address that challenge with a series of executive hires, international expansion efforts and channel partnerships aimed at supporting what the company views as a rapidly emerging enterprise security category.
Reco, which provides an AI security platform focused on discovering, governing and securing AI agents, identities and SaaS connections, announced several leadership appointments alongside new operations in Texas and the United Kingdom and Ireland. The company said the moves reflect accelerating demand from large enterprises seeking governance infrastructure for AI deployments.
More than 100 enterprises are currently using the platform as organizations move beyond experimentation and begin deploying AI agents at scale, according to the company.
Among the leadership additions is Zoe Hillenmeyer, who has been appointed chief operating officer. Hillenmeyer joins Reco from Protect AI, where she led commercial and marketing functions focused on AI security. Her previous experience also includes leadership roles at AWS, IBM and Peak AI. At Reco, she will oversee go-to-market execution, operational scaling and cross-functional alignment as the company expands its enterprise presence.
“I joined Reco because the company is solving the right problem at exactly the right moment,” Hillenmeyer said. “Agent governance is where identity security and AI risk converge, and most enterprises do not yet have the infrastructure to manage it.”
The company also named Kristen Twining senior vice president of Americas sales and business development. Twining previously served as senior vice president of sales for the Americas at FireMon, where she focused on enterprise cybersecurity engagements. Her responsibilities at Reco include overseeing sales operations across the Americas, driving pipeline growth and expanding the company’s presence in the mid-market segment.
Additional appointments include Dana Harduf as chief human resources officer, Sandy Mathews as vice president of product marketing and Merav Keren Kindler as vice president of marketing.
To support customer growth, Reco is opening a physical office in Texas, where it already maintains employees and serves enterprise customers. The company cited the state’s concentration of Fortune 500 headquarters, particularly within financial services, healthcare and energy, as a key factor in the expansion. Those sectors are among the most active in adopting AI technologies while navigating increasingly complex identity and governance requirements.
Reco is also expanding internationally with a dedicated team in the United Kingdom and Ireland. The company said demand has increased as European organizations prepare for compliance requirements associated with the European Union’s AI regulatory framework. Oliver Sears has joined the company as UKI sales director and will lead enterprise sales efforts across the region.
The expansion comes as enterprises seek greater visibility into how AI agents interact with applications, data and user identities. Reco’s platform uses a knowledge graph architecture to map identities, permissions, connectivity and activity across enterprise environments in real time. The company says the platform supports more than 235 applications and includes more than 1,000 detection controls designed to identify security and governance risks.
In addition to its direct sales efforts, Reco reported progress within its channel ecosystem. The company said it has achieved top national reseller rankings with a key U.S. channel partner that has developed a managed security services practice built around Reco’s platform. The partnership delivers AI agent governance and identity security services to enterprise customers and reflects growing interest among service providers seeking differentiated offerings around AI security.
Customer adoption has also helped increase the company’s visibility within enterprise security organizations.
“What surprised me most was how painless it was — and that’s thanks to Reco,” said Aaron Ansari, chief information security officer at Exela Pharma Sciences. “To have a solution that was able to come in and give us, almost instantly, within days, the true understanding of our footprint and our environment was very surprising in a positive way.”
The company recently received three Global InfoSec Awards for 2026, including recognition in SaaS and cloud security, AI security solutions and generative AI cybersecurity categories.
“AI agent security is no longer a planning-cycle conversation for Fortune 100 security teams,” said Reco Chief Executive Officer Ofer Klein. “It is an active deployment challenge.”
As enterprises continue integrating AI into business processes, Reco is betting that governance and identity security will become foundational infrastructure requirements. The company’s latest executive appointments, geographic expansion and partner investments are designed to support that shift as organizations move from AI experimentation to large-scale deployment.
